name: Bit tricks
tagline: x ^ x is 0, and x & (x - 1) drops the lowest 1.
signals: every value appears twice except one
template:
def count_ones(n):
    count = 0
    while n:
        n &= n - 1        # clears the lowest set bit
        count += 1
    return count

print(count_ones(13), bin(13))  # -> 3 0b1101
complexity: O(1) per operation, O(number of bits) per loop

blocks.html: A row of light switches: each bit is on or off. Bit tricks flip, test and count those switches with single CPU operations, and need no extra memory.

blocks.text: Example: the one value without a pair

blocks.note: Count every value, then XOR everything together

blocks.html: XOR is its own undo: x ^ x == 0 and x ^ 0 == x, in any order. XOR everything, every pair cancels, and the odd one is left.

blocks.why: 12 is 1100 and 11 is 1011. n & (n - 1) clears the lowest 1 of 12, leaving 1000 = 8.

pitfalls: Python ints never overflow. Mask with & 0xFFFFFFFF when the problem means 32-bit numbers.
n >> 1 on a negative number never reaches 0. Loop a fixed 32 times instead of while n.
bin(n) returns a string with a 0b prefix (and -0b for negatives). Slice it off before you count or pad.
